item.title: Generative AI Project Template with FastAPI, NiceGUI, and Ollama
item.description:
Generative AI Project Template with FastAPI, NiceGUI, and Ollama

A new generative‑AI project template combines FastAPI, NiceGUI and Ollama for rapid prototyping.

🔍 Overview

  • FastAPI backend and NiceGUI frontend for chat.
  • Local Ollama or cloud models through LiteLLM.
  • uv workspace tooling, tests, Docker Compose and GitHub releases.
  • Requires Make, Bash, Git and uv.

🧩 How it Works

  • Clone the repo: git clone https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template.git.
  • Navigate into it: cd generative-ai-project-template.
  • Install dev tools: make install-dev.
  • Copy the example env: cp .env.example .env.
  • Configure INFERENCE_* and EMBEDDINGS_* in .env for your model provider.
  • Start the app: make run.
  • Open the frontend at http://localhost:8080 or the backend API docs at http://localhost:8000/docs.
  • For local Ollama: make install-ollama then make run-with-ollama.

⚙️ Key Details

  • make docker-compose – Backend, frontend and Ollama in containers; Compose 2.24+.
  • make docker-compose-cuda – Same stack with GPU access for Ollama; NVIDIA drivers required.
  • make docker-compose-rebuild – Rebuild containers after source changes.
  • make run-backend / make run-frontend – Start either application separately.
  • Python PyTorch extras are optional for model development; Ollama inference runs outside Python.
  • make install-dev installs Git hooks in a checkout; make pre-commit-install reinstalls them.
  • make test-local runs offline tests.
  • Before a PR, configure the integration services and run make check – includes live LLM/Ollama/API tests.
  • make help lists all targets.
  • make deploy-doc-local previews documentation.
  • uv provisions the Python version set by requires‑python in pyproject.toml.

🚀 Availability

  • Repository: https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template.
  • Local frontend: http://localhost:8080.
  • Backend API docs: http://localhost:8000/docs.

#FastAPI #NiceGUI #Ollama #Docker #Python

item.title: Graham Dumpleton Releases Wrapture Monkey Patching Library for Python
item.description:
Graham Dumpleton Releases Wrapture Monkey Patching Library for Python

Graham Dumpleton has released wrapture, a monkey patching library designed for both testing and observability, with new tutorials and documentation published since its initial release on August 31st.

🔍 Overview

Wrapture is alpha software that serves as a tool for Python developers to handle testing and New Relic style tracing simultaneously. It is described as a “Swiss Army Knife” package for solving various problems.

⚙️ Key details

Developers can use wrapture for several specific functions:

  • Unit Testing: Used for similar purposes as unittest.mock.
  • Call Recording: Recording method calls as timelines and displaying them as trees.
  • Phased Behaviour: Arranging patched methods to change behavior across multiple calls.
  • Attribute Patching: Monkey patching dictionaries, generators, and attributes beyond just callables.
  • Tracing: Live tracing of applications and “zero-code tracing” via a separate TOML file that requires no modification of Python code.
  • Performance Analysis: Tools for recording timing information, both individually and aggregated across multiple calls.
  • Exporting: Exporting traces to OpenTelemetry.

🧩 Instrumentation Support

The separate wrapture-instrumenation package provides instrumentation for the following:

Target Support
Web Frameworks flask, fastapi, django, starlette
HTTP Clients/Servers requests, httpx, http.client, urllib.request, urllib3, aiohttp.client, aiohttp.web, uvicorn, werkzeug.serving, wsgiref.simple_server
Databases/Data sqlalchemy, sqlite3
Other grpc, jinja2, xmlrpc.client, xmlrpc.server

🚀 Availability

In addition to the library, Graham Dumpleton has provided a set of interactive workshops implemented as JupyterLab notebooks.

#Python #wrapture #monkeypatching #observability #softwaretesting

Source: Don’t sleep on wrapture
